title: The chairman's car
summary: Your car's in the garage, and the chairman throws you the keys to his for the week. It's old and very, very clean. A season on, he wants to know who scratched it.

ends.title: Owned up
ends.text: You put a scratch on the chairman's old car and told him. He still lends it to you.

ends.title: The scratch
ends.text: Somebody put a scratch on the chairman's old car. He still asks about it.

beats.title: The keys

event.title: The keys
event.speaker: chairman
setup: Your car's in the garage until Friday. {chairman.short} walks past in the car park and throws you a set of keys on a leather fob. "Have mine. I've got the wife's. Don't touch the radio."

say: It's thirty years old, cream, with leather seats and a smell of polish. On Thursday, in the training ground car park, you reverse it into the bollard by the bins. There's a scratch on the back bumper the length of your finger.

replies.label: Give the keys back and say nothing.

tell.text: He's quiet for a long time on the phone. Then he says he did the same thing in 1994, to the bollard by the bins. He pays for it himself.

fix.text: A man in an industrial unit fixes it for two weeks' wages, cash, and the colour is nearly right.

hide.text: You give him the keys back on Friday with a thank you card. He finds it on Saturday.

beats.hint: The chairman lends you his car

event.title: The bollard
event.speaker: chairman
setup: A season on. The car park. {chairman.short} is standing by the bollard by the bins with his hands in his pockets.
{if arc.path=='told'}"Do you want the car again? Mine's free on Tuesday. Mind the bollard."{/if}
{if !arc.path=='told'}"Somebody touched my car last season. I've had a year to think about who."{/if}

outcomes.text: "I know. I just wanted to hear it." He throws you the keys again.
"I know, you daft lad. Tuesday." He throws you the keys.
He looks at you, then at the bollard. "Hm." He walks off.
"Tuesday, then." He throws you the keys anyway.
